summary: Archaeology Magazine: external ramp and crane theories have serious flaws; Houdin internal ramp theory presented with microgravimetry and notch evidence.
content: Herodotus (c.450 BC) mentioned 'machines' (cranes); Diodorus of Sicily wrote 'mounds' (ramps). Single ramp would be ~1 mile long, no room on Giza plateau, volume as great as pyramid. Corkscrew ramp obscures corners for surveyors (Dieter Arnold). Crane theory: shadouf devices, but too much timber needed and no place for cranes near top. Houdin internal ramp: external ramp for bottom third, internal ramp 6ft wide 7% grade for top two-thirds; corner notches for turning blocks; 1986 French microgravimetry survey showed density image matching internal ramp prediction.
